comparison.objective: Selectively reject marked cartons from a moving line while leaving good cartons undisturbed; candidate likewise selectively rejects defective cartons from a moving belt while good cartons continue.
comparison.physical_skill: Both test state-conditioned intervention on moving cartons without disturbing acceptable neighbors. PR-1217 requires lateral pushing and expressly forbids lifting; candidate requires moving-target body capture, flap avoidance, lifting and spill-free transport of loose contents.
comparison.success_condition: Both require rejects off the line in a reject area and good cartons preserved on their original path, with whole-trial shortcut penalties. Candidate adds retained free contents, open-state semantics, full body clearance, guarded release and 3 s dwell; PR-1217 requires a low straight-across push route and 1 s success hold.
comparison.reason: The core tested objective and policy distinction—remove selected cartons from a live line while leaving good cartons on it—substantially overlap. Flaps, contents and mandatory lifting add real dexterity, but extend an existing selective moving-line rejection ability rather than replacing it with an unrelated one.
